'''Bradford Scott Lander''' (born July 8, 1969)<ref>{{cite tweet |last1=Lander |first1=Brad |date=July 8, 2022 |title=My run in on Wednesday before the ferry audit release: fortifying. My run in today to kick off my 53rd birthday: sublime. |user=bradlander |number=1545384834838798339 |access-date=June 18, 2025}}</ref> is an American politician and urban planner who is the [[U.S. Representative|U.S. Representative-elect]] for [[New York's 10th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/new-york-us-house-district-10-results |title=New York House District 10 General Election Results 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref> A [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] Democrat, he previously served as [[New York City Comptroller|New York City comptroller]] from 2022 until 2025, and before that served on the [[New York City Council]] from 2010 to 2021, representing the [[New York City's 39th City Council district|39th district]], which is partly based in [[Brooklyn]].

Born in suburban [[St. Louis]], Lander has pursued his political career in [[New York City]] since the 1990s, where he has become a mainstay in progressive activism.<ref name="Barkan2025">{{Cite web |last=Barkan |first=Ross |date=December 12, 2025 |title=A Very Interesting Primary Is Brewing in Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/brad-lander-vs-dan-goldman-will-be-a-popcorn-worthy-primary.html |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=Intelligencer |language=en}}</ref> In 2009, Lander was elected to the city council, serving until his election as comptroller in [[2021 New York City Comptroller election|2021]]. In [[2025 New York City mayoral election|2025]], Lander unsuccessfully ran for [[Mayor of New York City|New York City mayor]], placing third in the Democratic primary.<ref name="Fitzsimmons-2024">{{Cite news |last=Fitzsimmons |first=Emma G. |date=July 30, 2024 |title=Brad Lander, New York City's Comptroller, Will Run Against Mayor Adams |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/07/30/nyregion/brad-lander-mayor-adams.html |access-date=July 31, 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
[[File:Bradford Lander 1987.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.8|150px|Lander in the [[Parkway North High School]] yearbook, 1987]]
Brad Lander is the son of Carole Lander and David Lander, a bankruptcy attorney.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stljewishlight.com/features/profiles/david-lander-a-decades-long-pursuit-of-social-justice/article_5b3f0c52-6044-11e8-94f9-9bf7be18e147.html|title=David Lander: A decades-long pursuit of social justice|date=May 25, 2018|first1=David|last1=Baugher|website=St. Louis Jewish Light}}</ref> He grew up in [[Creve Coeur, Missouri|Creve Coeur]], a suburb of [[St. Louis]], Missouri, in a [[Reform Judaism|Reform Jewish]] family,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heybk.nyc/new-blog/2019/5/26/s3-e4-brad-lander-nyc-council-district-39-transcript|title=S3 &#124; E4 &#124; Brad Lander, NYC Council, District 39|website=Hey BK Podcast|date=January 2, 2020}}</ref><ref name= "Taylor2014">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/24/nyregion/unassuming-liberal-suddenly-becomes-council-kingmaker.html|title=An Unassuming Liberal Makes a Rapid Ascent to Power Broker|first=Kate|last=Taylor|date=January 23, 2014|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref name="Nathan-Kazis-2017">{{cite web|url=https://forward.com/news/365134/brad-lander-is-face-of-anti-trump-resistance-and-keeps-brooklyn-orthodox-ha/|title=How Face Of Anti-Trump Resistance Keeps Orthodox Happy, Too|website=The Forward |first1=Josh|last1=Nathan-Kazis|date=March 15, 2017}}</ref> and graduated from [[Parkway North High School]] in 1987.<ref name="Parkway">{{cite web|url=https://mo01931486.schoolwires.net/cms/lib/MO01931486/Centricity/Domain/1466/August%202024%20Newsletter.pdf|title=Parkway Alumni Association Newsletter|date=August 2024}}</ref>

Lander developed an early interest in political issues, and was strongly influenced by the example set by the [[civil rights]] and [[anti-Vietnam War movement|anti-war]] leaders [[Reverend]] [[Martin Luther King Jr.]] and [[Rabbi]] [[Abraham Joshua Heschel]].<ref name="Taylor2014" /> As a teenager he helped organize a march in [[Washington, D.C.]] in support of [[History of the Jews in the Soviet Union|Jews in the Soviet Union]] who [[Refusenik|were not allowed to emigrate]].<ref name="Taylor2014" />

Lander earned a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1991, where he received a [[Harry S. Truman Scholarship]] and joined the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).<ref name="Taylor2014"/><ref name=Kornbluh>{{Cite news |title=Who would protect New York Jews better? Cuomo and Lander trade attacks on the campaign trail |first=Jacob |last=Kornbluh |date=April 2, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Forward]] |url=https://forward.com/news/709078/andrew-cuomo-nyc-mayoral-race-lander/}}</ref> He earned a master's degree in [[anthropology]] from [[University College London]] on a [[Marshall Scholarship]], followed by a master's degree in [[urban planning]] from the [[Pratt Institute]] in New York.<ref name="BKLNER Comptroller">{{cite web |last1=Goba |first1=Kadia |date=April 8, 2019 |title=Could Brad Lander Be the City's Next Comptroller? |url=https://bklyner.com/could-brad-lander-be-the-citys-next-comptroller/ |work=[[Bklyner]]}}</ref>

==Early career==
From 1993 to 2003, Lander was the executive director of the Fifth Avenue Committee (FAC), a [[Park Slope]] nonprofit organization that develops and manages [[Affordable housing in the United States|affordable housing]].<ref name="leadershipforchange.org">{{cite web|url=http://www.leadershipforchange.org/awardees/awardee.php3?ID=46|title=2002 Award Recipients; Fifth Avenue Committee|publisher=Leadership for a Changing World|date=August 12, 2001|access-date=October 20, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930131230/http://www.leadershipforchange.org/awardees/awardee.php3?ID=46|archive-date=September 30, 2011}}</ref><ref name= "Taylor2014"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://therealdeal.com/2021/01/06/lander-seeks-to-keep-for-profit-developers-from-acquiring-city-owned-land/|title=Brad Lander NYC Council Bill Seeks to Boost Nonprofit Developers|date=January 6, 2021|website=[[The Real Deal (magazine)|The Real Deal New York]]|first1=Kathryn|last1=Brenzel}}</ref>

From 2003 to 2009, Lander was a director of the university-based [[Pratt Center for Community Development]]. In that position, he was a critic of the [[Bloomberg administration]]'s development policies.<ref name= "Taylor2014"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pratt.edu/newsite/print.php?div_id=4637|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071031043713/http://www.pratt.edu/newsite/print.php?div_id=4637|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 31, 2007|title=faculty profiles / Brad Lander|publisher=Pratt Institute|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rooflines.org/members/114|title=About Brad Lander – National Housing Institute|publisher=Rooflines|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsday.com/long-island/bloomberg-reshapes-city-despite-high-profile-setbacks-1.880919|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605134841/http://www.newsday.com/long-island/bloomberg-reshapes-city-despite-high-profile-setbacks-1.880919|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 5, 2011|title=Bloomberg reshapes city, despite high profile setbacks|work=[[Newsday]]|first1=David|last1=Freedlander|location=New York|date=April 10, 2008|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref> He has also been a critic of the [[Atlantic Yards]] project.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bernstein|first=Andrea|url=http://www.wnyc.org/news/articles/51689|title=Developer Has Mixed Record in Brooklyn|publisher=[[WNYC]]|date=September 13, 2005|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref> Lander served on a mayoral taskforce that recommended reforms to the [[421-a tax exemption]] for luxury housing and required that new development in certain areas of the city set aside affordable housing units.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.prattcenter.net/projects/sustainable-community-development/reforming-nycs-421-property-tax-exemption-program|website=Pratt Center for Community Development|title=Reforming NYC's 421-a Property Tax Exemption Program|access-date=September 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first11=Adam|last1=Lisberg|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/real-estate-board-hammerin-old-tax-breaks-article-1.389673|title=Real estate board is hammerin' for old tax breaks|work=[[New York Daily News]]|location=New York|date=February 8, 2009|access-date=September 3, 2018}}</ref> He co-led the completion of the One City One Future platform, a progressive vision for economic development in New York City.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://onecityonefuture.org|title=Travel and Car Rentals|publisher=Onecityonefuture.org|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wnyc.org/shows/bl/episodes/2009/05/12/segments/131656|title=The Brian Lehrer Show: One City/One Future|publisher=[[WNYC]]|date=May 12, 2009|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref> He stepped down as head of the organization in 2009 to seek a seat on the [[New York City Council]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://prattcenter.net/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090810164656/http://prattcenter.net/staff/brad-lander|url-status=dead|title=Homepage|archive-date=August 10, 2009|website=Pratt Center for Community Development}}</ref> Lander teaches as an adjunct professor at [[Brooklyn Law School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brooklaw.edu/Contact-Us/Lander%20Brad|title= Lander Brad|publisher=[[Brooklyn Law School]]}}</ref>

== New York City Council ==
[[File:Brad Lander 2010.jpg|thumb|right|Lander in 2010]]

Lander represented the 39th district on the New York City Council from 2009 until 2021, when term limits prevented him from running again. He co-founded the [[Progressive Caucus in the New York City Council]].<ref name="Taylor2014"/> In his first term, Lander co-chaired the caucus with Speaker [[Melissa Mark-Viverito]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Chen|first=David W.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/24/nyregion/24council.html|title=12 New York City Council Members Form Liberal Bloc|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 23, 2010|access-date=October 20, 2011}}</ref>

In 2009, Lander ran to represent the 39th district on the New York City Council, including the Brooklyn neighborhoods of [[Boerum Hill]], [[Borough Park, Brooklyn|Borough Park]], [[Brooklyn Heights]], [[Carroll Gardens]], [[Cobble Hill, Brooklyn|Cobble Hill]], [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Flatbush]], [[Gowanus]], [[Green-Wood Cemetery]], [[Kensington, Brooklyn|Kensington]], [[Park Slope]], [[Prospect Heights, Brooklyn|Prospect Heights]], [[Prospect Lefferts Gardens]], [[Red Hook, Brooklyn|Red Hook]], [[Prospect Park (Brooklyn)|Prospect Park]], [[South Slope]], [[Sunset Park, Brooklyn|Sunset Park]], and [[Windsor Terrace]].<ref>{{cite web |date=November 16, 2007 |title=Housing Advocate Brad Lander to Run for DeBlasio's Council Spot – Daily Intel |url=https://nymag.com/daily/intel/2007/11/housing_advocate_brad_lander_t.html |access-date=October 20, 2011 |work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]}}</ref> He won the Democratic primary on September 15, 2009, with 41% of the vote in a field of five and appeared on the general election ballot on the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and [[Working Families Party]] lines.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 16, 2009 |title=In the 39th District: Lander crushes four rivals |url=https://www.brooklynpaper.com/stories/32/37/32_37_gk_39th_district_primary_results.html |access-date=October 20, 2011 |work=[[The Brooklyn Paper]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111125115851/https://www.brooklynpaper.com/stories/32/37/32_37_gk_39th_district_primary_results.html |archive-date=November 25, 2011}}</ref> On November 4, 2009, he won with 70% of the vote. After his first four-year term, Lander was reelected on the Democratic and Working Families Parties' lines in 2013.

== New York City comptroller ==

=== 2021 election ===
{{main|2021 New York City Comptroller election}}
[[File:Brad Lander Loren Michelle Pablo Forever Mural May-8-2021.jpg|thumb|Brad Lander and skateboarding advocate Loren Michelle pose in front of the [[Pablo Forever]] Mural at [[Washington Park (Brooklyn)|Washington Skatepark]] in Park Slope on May 8, 2021.]]

Facing term limits for his council seat after his third term, Lander announced his candidacy for the [[2021 New York City Comptroller election]],<ref name="GG Comptroller" /><ref name="BKLNER Comptroller" /> an open race as the incumbent, [[Scott Stringer]], also faced term limits.<ref name="GG Comptroller" /><ref name="BKLNER Comptroller" /> He said that if elected he would expand the office to conduct equity audits to reduce disparities across race, gender, and ethnicity, including in how city agencies hire contractors.<ref name="Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club-2021" /> He said he would also use the office as an organizing vehicle for advocates, and produce audits, draft reports, and release data in partnership with organizers running campaigns centered on racial, social, and economic justice.<ref name="Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club-2021" /> Lander was endorsed by the [[Working Families Party]], unions including [[Communications Workers of America]] District 1, and various Democratic clubs and community organizations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.landerfornyc.com/endorsements|title=Endorsements|author=Brad Lander for NYC Comptroller|access-date=May 4, 2021}}</ref> He was endorsed by progressive elected officials including Senator [[Elizabeth Warren]], Public Advocate [[Jumaane Williams]], Congresswoman [[Nydia Velázquez]], Congresswoman [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], and members of the New York City Council and New York State legislature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/states/new-york/albany/story/2021/04/15/public-advocate-jumaane-williams-endorses-brad-lander-for-comptroller-1375203|title=Jumaane Williams endorses Brad Lander for comptroller|first=Jonathan|last=Custodio|work=[[Politico]]|date=April 15, 2021|access-date=May 7, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/news/politics/us-elections-government/ny-brad-lander-controller-nydia-velazquez-20210417-vkh7jwbzgbdzbh4tmkztybwqpi-story.html|title=Brad Lander wins endorsement of Rep. Nydia Velazquez in crowded NYC comptroller race|first=Dave|last=Goldiner|work=The New York Daily News|date=April 17, 2021|access-date=May 7, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/31/nyregion/aoc-endorsement-brad-lander.html|title=Ocasio-Cortez Endorses Brad Lander in N.Y.C. Comptroller's Race|first=Dave|last=Goldiner|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 31, 2021|access-date=May 7, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Glueck |first1=Katie |last2=Rubinstein |first2=Dana |date=April 10, 2021 |title='Sense of Disappointment' on the Left as the N.Y.C. Mayor's Race Unfolds |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/10/nyregion/yang-adams-mayor-progressives.html |access-date=May 5, 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

Lander won the Democratic primary against State Senator [[Brian Benjamin]], entrepreneur and former US Marine [[Zach Iscol]], New York State Senator [[Kevin Parker (New York politician)|Kevin Parker]], former Public Advocate and former New York City Council Speaker [[Corey Johnson (politician)|Corey Johnson]], and New York State Assemblymember [[David Weprin]], among others,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mays |first=Jeffery C. |date=January 27, 2021 |title=One Candidate Leaves Crowded Mayor's Race. One From 'Housewives' Joins. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/27/nyregion/zach-iscol-mayor-comptroller.html |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> and won the general election over Republican nominee Daby Carreras.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sommerfeldt |first1=Chris |last2=Balk |first2=Tim |date=November 3, 2021 |title=Lander, Williams Stroll to Victories |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/daily-news-lander-williams-stroll-to-vi/148861454/ |access-date=June 6, 2024 |newspaper=[[New York Daily News]] |page=4 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

=== Tenure ===
In 2022, Lander called for ending [[421-a tax exemption|421a]], a program that provided tax incentives for developers of market-rate apartments who also added below-market rentals.<ref name="Haag-2022">{{Cite news |last=Haag |first=Matthew |date=May 26, 2022 |title=Why a Lucrative Tax Break for Developers Is Likely to Die in Albany |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/26/nyregion/tax-exemption-housing-development.html |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Lander and other critics described it as a subsidy for developers in exchange for few low-income units, while supporters argued that it encouraged housing construction and alleviated the housing shortage in New York.<ref name="Haag-2022" />

In March 2022, Lander called on Mayor [[Eric Adams]] to abandon his effort to shift retired municipal workers onto a new [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] program and comply with a court order declaring the move illegal.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.nydailynews.com/news/politics/new-york-elections-government/ny-nyc-comptroller-lander-mayor-adams-medicare-plan-city-retirees-20220308-im4d7kk3gvcappzlctlvxsfd2u-story.html | title=Comptroller Lander calls on Mayor Adams to ditch new NYC retiree Medicare plan after court order | website=[[New York Daily News]] | last=Sommerfeldt | first=Chris | date=March 8, 2022 }}</ref> He subsequently refused to register the city's contract with [[Aetna]], citing pending legislation that called the program's legality into question, but Adams overrode his decision and registered the contract.<ref name="medicare">{{Cite web | url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/policy/2024/12/city-retirees-win-court-again-adams-vows-press/401781/ | first = Bob| last = Hennelly |title=City retirees win in court again, as Adams vows to press on | website=City & State New York | date=December 19, 2024 }}</ref>

Lander developed a reputation as a [[Foil (narrative)|foil]] to Adams, often criticizing or using the comptroller's oversight role to challenge his policies.<ref name="POLITICO">{{Cite web |last=Anuta |first=Joe |date=July 6, 2023 |title=NYC's mayor has found his archrival. His name is Brad Lander. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/07/06/nyc-eric-adams-brad-lander-00104669 |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=[[Politico]]}}</ref> In 2023, ''Politico'' called Lander Adams's "archrival".<ref name="POLITICO" /> In February 2025, Lander released a public letter to Adams threatening to convene a meeting of the [[Inability Committee]] if Adams did not "develop and present a detailed contingency plan outlining how you intend to manage the City of New York."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russo-Lennon |first=Barbara |date=February 17, 2025 |title=City Council Speaker Adrienne Adams reacts to City Hall's mass resignations |url=https://www.amny.com/news/speaker-adams-mayor-adams-resign-lander-02172025/ |access-date=February 17, 2025 |website=[[AM New York Metro]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lander is a member of the Vote Blue Coalition, a progressive group and [[Political action committee#Non-connected PACs|federal PAC]] created to support Democrats in New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania through voter outreach and mobilization efforts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coalition |url=https://votebluenyc.org/coalition/ |access-date=July 17, 2024 |website=Vote Blue |language=en}}</ref>

{{main|ICE and New York City during the second Trump presidency}}

In June 2025, as Donald Trump [[Immigration policy of the second Donald Trump administration|increased deportations of immigrants]], Lander began accompanying defendants to immigration hearings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rivlin-Nadler |first=Max |date=June 5, 2025 |title=NYC Comptroller Brad Lander Walks With Immigrants Outside Court to Shield Them From ICE:'I Would Urge New Yorkers to Do This' |url=https://hellgatenyc.com/lander-accompanies-immigrants-ice/ |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=Hellgate |language=en-us}}</ref> On June 17, Lander was arrested and handcuffed by masked [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) officials at an immigration court while linking arms with a person ICE was trying to detain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shivonne |first=Adeja |date=June 17, 2025 |title=NYC mayoral candidate Brad Lander arrested by ICE, spokesperson says |url=https://www.fox5ny.com/news/nyc-mayoral-candidate-arrest-ice-spokesperson-says |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=FOX 5 NY |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Amatulli2025">{{Cite web |last=Amatulli |first=Jenna |date=June 17, 2025 |title=New York City comptroller Brad Lander arrested at immigration court hearing |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jun/17/brad-lander-arrested-new-york-city-comptroller |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Attanasio |first=Cedar |date=June 17, 2025 |title=NYC mayoral candidate is arrested at immigration court after linking arms with man being detained |url=https://apnews.com/article/brad-lander-nyc-immigration-court-arrest-6ed341297efab31a08a14421674d8ed8 |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en}}</ref> The reason given for the arrest was "assaulting law enforcement and impeding a federal officer", according to [[United States Department of Homeland Security|Department of Homeland Security]] spokeswoman [[Tricia McLaughlin (government official)|Tricia McLaughlin]]. Lander was released and said he "certainly did not" assault an officer.<ref name="Amatulli2025"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Faguy |first=Ana |date=June 17, 2025 |title=NYC mayoral candidate Brad Lander arrested by ICE |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvg430dx702o |access-date=June 18, 2025 |website=[[BBC]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ferré-Sadurní |first=Luis |date=June 17, 2025 |title=Brad Lander, NYC Mayoral Candidate, Arrested by ICE Agents at Immigration Courthouse |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/17/nyregion/brad-lander-immigration-ice.html |access-date=June 17, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The arrest was condemned by Democratic politicians from the state, including [[Governor of New York|New York State Governor]] [[Kathy Hochul]], [[Attorney General of New York|NYS Attorney General]] [[Letitia James]], and [[U.S. Representative]] Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Lucy |last2=Dunbar |first2=Marina |last3=Clinton |first3=Jane |date=June 17, 2025 |title=New York politicians condemn mayoral candidate Brad Lander's arrest as 'fascism' and 'political intimidation' – US politics live |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2025/jun/17/donald-trump-g7-iran-israel-ceasefire-us-politics-live-updates |access-date=June 17, 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Lander was arrested by DHS again on September 18, along with several New York state legislators while trying to access ICE detention cells and protest the detentions at the [[Jacob K. Javits Federal Building]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hogan |first1=Gwynne |title=Homeland Security Arrests Brad Lander and 10 State Lawmakers Inside 26 Federal Plaza |url=https://www.thecity.nyc/2025/09/18/dhs-arrests-brad-lander-democratic-lawmakers-26-federal-plaza/ |website=The City |access-date=September 18, 2025 |date=September 18, 2025}}</ref> In a two-day bench trial in June 2026, Lander was found not guilty of obstructing officers' access to an elevator.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Zanger |first1=Jesse |last2=Gainer |first2=Alice |title=Brad Lander found not guilty in trial over immigration court arrest |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/brad-lander-guilty-immigration-court-arrest/ |date=June 11, 2026 |work=CBS}}</ref>

In 2025, advocacy organization [[New York Communities for Change]] (NYCC) representatives voiced frustration with Lander and the New York City Comptroller's Office in regard to helping keep solvent three pension funds for retirees of various New York City employers: the New York City Employees Retirement System, the New York City Teachers Retirement System, and the New York City Board of Education Retirement System. The Comptroller's office is supposed to determine which [[asset management]] companies are environmentally friendly and reject investing city employees' retirement funds in companies that have a poor record. NYCC and other environmental groups argued that Lander was stalling his office's investigation into controversial investment company [[BlackRock]] in order to delay divesting from it. NYCC threatened to stop endorsing Lander in his next campaign because he missed a September 2025 deadline to respond to its representatives.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/policy/2025/11/lander-spars-progressive-activist-group-previously-backed-him/409345/|title=Lander spars with progressive activist group that previously backed him|first=Celia|last=Bernhardt|date=November 5, 2025|website=City & State NY}}</ref>

== 2025 New York City mayoral campaign ==
{{Main|2025 New York City Democratic mayoral primary}}

[[File:2025 New York City Democratic primary mayoral election first round (Lander vote share).svg|thumb|Map of Lander's vote share in the first round of the Democratic primary by precinct and borough]]
[[File:GogolP1076070 02.jpg|thumb|Lander at [[Gogol Bordello]]'s show at [[Prospect Park (Brooklyn)|Prospect Park]] shortly after the election]]
In July 2024, Lander announced that he would challenge incumbent [[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] [[Eric Adams]] in the [[2025 New York City mayoral election]].<ref name="Fitzsimmons-2024" />

On June 12, 2025, ''[[The New York Times]]'' Opinion panel chose Lander as its top choice for the Democratic primary for mayor.<ref name="The New York Times-2025">{{Cite news |date=June 12, 2025 |title=Opinion {{!}} Who Should Lead New York? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/06/12/opinion/nyc-mayor-election-candidates.html |access-date=June 19, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> According to the Opinion editors, the panel consisted of 15 New Yorkers, chosen based on their "experience in citywide or local community affairs, their knowledge of key issues, and their range of viewpoints."<ref name="The New York Times-2025" /> Panelists noted Lander's extensive experience and accomplishments in city government, his demonstrated ability to listen and evolve on issues, his history of uniting opposing groups on housing and other issues, and his "smart instincts" as being among his strengths.<ref name="The New York Times-2025" /> They defined his "integrity, competence and consensus building" as three crucial qualities for leadership, and his responsibility and efficiency were highlighted even by panelists who preferred other candidates.<ref name="The New York Times-2025" /> The panel praised his policy stances, as well as what they described as his "capacity to manage New York's sprawling bureaucracy" and "detailed knowledge of city government and finances."<ref name="The New York Times-2025" /> He was journalist [[Ezra Klein]]'s top choice in the [[2025 New York City Democratic mayoral primary|Democratic primary]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 18, 2025 |title=Opinion {{!}} This Is Brad Lander's New York |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/18/opinion/mayor-lander-gowanus-cuomo-mamdani.html |access-date=July 29, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

On June 13, 2025, Lander and [[Zohran Mamdani]] cross-endorsed each other in the Democratic primary.<ref>{{Cite web| last=Fitzsimmons |first=Emma |date=June 13, 2025 |title= Mamdani and Lander Cross-Endorse Each Other in N.Y.C. Mayor's Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/13/nyregion/mamdani-lander-endorsement-nyc-mayor.html |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-us}}</ref> Lander placed third in the first round and was eliminated immediately thereafter.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

Lander was expected to play a large role in Zohran Mamdani's transition team<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/11/05/nyc-mayor-elect-zohran-mamdani-transition-team/87108212007/|title=Zohran Mamdani, now NYC mayor-elect, announces mainstream transition team. Who's on it?|first=Eduardo|last=Cuevas|date=November 5, 2025|website=USA TODAY}}</ref> but instead focused on local politics, according to [[Politico]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/10/mamdani-picks-his-top-two-city-hall-deputies-00644783|title=Mamdani picks his top 2 City Hall deputies|date=November 10, 2025|last=Coltin|first=Jeff|website=POLITICO}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that Mamdani met with Lander in October 2025 to discuss the latter challenging incumbent member of the United States House [[Dan Goldman]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New York|2026]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |last2=Benjamin |first2=Oreskes |date=November 14, 2025 |title=The Strategic Uncoupling of Zohran Mamdani and Brad Lander |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/14/nyregion/mamdani-lander-dan-goldman.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=November 15, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

On December 10, 2025, Lander announced his candidacy for [[New York's 10th congressional district]], attempting to primary moderate incumbent [[Dan Goldman]] from the left. He was endorsed by New York City mayor [[Zohran Mamdani]], U.S. Senator [[Elizabeth Warren]], U.S. Senator [[Bernie Sanders]], New York City Public Advocate [[Jumaane Williams]], and the [[Working Families Party]].<ref name="Barkan2025" /><ref name="NYTimes 2025-12-10">{{Cite web |last=Fitzsimmons |first=Emma G. |date=December 10, 2025 |title=Lander Will Run for House Seat With Mamdani's Support |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/10/nyregion/lander-goldman-mamdani-congress.html |access-date=December 10, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> The district voted 60.3% in favor of Mamdani in the mayoral election and was Lander's strongest congressional district in the [[2025 New York City Democratic mayoral primary|Democratic mayoral primary]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apps.npr.org/2025-election-results/new-york.html|title=New York City mayoral election: 2025 live results|website=NPR}}</ref>

Despite his district overwhelmingly voting for Mamdani, Goldman did not endorse Mamdani during the mayoral election due to differences in opinion over Israel.<ref name="NYTimes 2025-12-10" /> After Lander announced his candidacy, other potential progressive challengers dropped out to bolster Lander's candidacy, including [[Alexa Avilés]], who had already received the support of the [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America]].<ref name="NYTimes 2025-12-10" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hogan |first=Gwynne |date=December 10, 2025 |title=Left Clears Lane for Brad Lander's Challenge to Rep. Dan Goldman |url=https://www.thecityreporter.nyc/2025/12/10/brad-lander-daniel-goldman-congress-10th-district/ |access-date=June 8, 2026 |work=[[The City Reporter]]}}</ref> On June 2, the pro-Palestine super PAC [[American Priorities]] announced that it would spend $2 million in support of a trio of progressive candidates in New York consisting of Lander as well as [[Darializa Avila Chevalier]] and [[Claire Valdez]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=King|first=Maya|last2=Fandos|first2=Nicholas|date=June 2, 2026|title=Group Pledges $2 Million to Fight AIPAC in House Races|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/02/nyregion/aipac-spending-campaign-super-pac.html|access-date=June 5, 2026|work=The New York Times|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Lander defeated Goldman 66 to 34% in the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026. New York's 10th district is considered a [[safe seat]] with a [[Cook Partisan Voting Index]] of D+26,<ref>{{cite web |title=PVI Map and District List |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/pvi-map-and-district-list |website=The Cook Political Report with [[Amy Walter]] |access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref> so Lander's win is considered tantamount to election.<ref>{{cite news |title=New York 10th Congressional District Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-new-york-us-house-10-primary.html |access-date=June 24, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=June 23, 2026}}</ref> The general election will take place on November 3, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=2026 Political Calendar |url=https://elections.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/12/2026-political-calendar-quad-fold-12.9.2025-final.pdf |website=[[New York State Board of Elections]] |access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref>

== Political positions ==
=== Participatory budgeting ===
Lander was one of four Council members who brought [[participatory budgeting]] to New York City, which allows citizens to propose, develop, and vote on items in the municipal budget.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/01/nyregion/for-some-new-yorkers-a-grand-experiment-in-participatory-budgeting.html|title=For Some New Yorkers, a Grand Experiment in Participatory Budgeting|last=Sangha|first=Soni|date=March 30, 2012|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=July 7, 2017|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> As of 2026, 22 of the 51 New York City Council Districts engage in participatory budgeting.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |last2= |date=May 22, 2026 |title=Speaker Julie Menin, New York City Council Members Announce Results of FY 2027 Participatory Budgeting |url=https://council.nyc.gov/press/2026/05/22/3126/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Press |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Labor ===
In 2013, Lander played a key role in a campaign to pass [[Sick leave in the United States|paid sick leave]] over Mayor Bloomberg's veto, telling the ''[[Brooklyn Reporter]]'' the legislation would "make our city a fairer, more compassionate place to live and work".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://brooklynreporter.com/2013/05/city-council-passes-paid-sick-leave-bill/|first=Terrence|last=Cullen|title=City Council passes paid sick leave bill|date=May 8, 2013|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=April 14, 2021}}</ref> In 2015, Lander passed legislation to ban discriminatory employment credit checks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/17/nyregion/new-york-city-council-votes-to-restrict-credit-checks-in-hiring.html|first=Nikita|last=Stewart|title=New York City Council Votes to Restrict Credit Checks in Hiring|date=April 6, 2015|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=April 14, 2021}}</ref> In March 2015, outside a Park Slope car wash that was closed at the time, Lander was arrested for blocking traffic to show support for eight striking car washers; it was his fourth arrest.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.metro.us/brooklyn-city-council-members-arrested-in-car-washers-protest/|first=Chester|last=Soria|title=Brooklyn city council members arrested in car washers protest|date= March 4, 2015|website=Metro US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://observer.com/2015/03/elected-officials-arrested-at-brooklyn-car-wash-rally/|title=Elected Officials Arrested at Brooklyn Car Wash Rally|date=March 4, 2015|work=[[The New York Observer|Observer]]| first=Ross|last=Barkan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/please-dont-arrest-meuntil-the-cameras-are-here-1506258001|title=Please Don't Arrest Me—Until the Cameras Are Here|first1=Mara|last1=Gay|first2=Mike|last2=Vilensky|first3=Zolan|last3=Kanno-Youngs|date=September 24, 2017|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref> In November 2016, he announced his intention to get arrested as part of the "[[Fight for $15]]" National Day of Action, saying it was "part of a long tradition of civil disobedience, and it takes a little courage".<ref name="arrested">{{cite web|url=https://www.thenation.com/article/archive/why-im-getting-arrested-during-todays-national-day-of-disruption/|title=Why I'm Getting Arrested During Today's National Day of Disruption|first=Brad|last=Lander|date=November 29, 2016|work=[[The Nation]]}}</ref>

Lander has crafted a number of workers' rights policies. In 2017, he passed legislation to require fast food and retail companies to give their workers stable scheduling and restrict on-call scheduling and last-minute changes.<ref>{{cite web |author=New York City Council |title=Int 1396 2016 |url=https://legistar.council.nyc.gov/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=2900942&GUID=F6382D3F-7D70-4324-A083-65BD4E355E55&Options=ID%7CText%7C&Search=fast+food}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Durkin |first=Erin |date=April 8, 2018 |title=City Council passes bill barring fast food chains from abruptly changing workers' schedules |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2017/05/24/city-council-passes-bill-barring-fast-food-chains-from-abruptly-changing-workers-schedules/ |work=[[New York Daily News]]}}</ref> Lander also sponsored a successful bill to prevent fast food workers from being fired without [[Just cause (employment law)|just cause]] and to allow them to appeal terminations through arbitration.<ref>{{cite web |last=de Freytas-Tamura |first=Kimiko |date=December 17, 2020 |title='No One Should Get Fired on a Whim': Fast Food Workers Win More Job Security |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/17/nyregion/nyc-fast-food-workers-job-security.html |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> He worked with the [[Freelancers Union]] to create the [[Freelance Isn't Free Act]], the first legislation of its kind to ensure that freelancers and independent contractors are paid fully and on time.<ref>{{cite web |first=Emma |last=Whitford |date=May 15, 2017 |title=NYC's 'Freelance Isn't Free' Act Goes Into Effect Today. |url=https://gothamist.com/news/nycs-freelance-isnt-free-act-goes-into-effect-today |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510143905/https://gothamist.com/news/nycs-freelance-isnt-free-act-goes-into-effect-today |archive-date=May 10, 2021 |access-date=May 6, 2021 |work=Next City}}</ref> In 2018, Lander achieved the first ruling in the country to guarantee a living wage for [[Uber]], [[Lyft]], and other for-hire drivers.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Holley |date=December 4, 2018 |title=New rules guarantee minimum wage for NYC Uber, Lyft drivers |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2018/12/04/new-rules-guarantee-minimum-wage-nyc-uber-lyft-drivers/ |access-date=April 21, 2021 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

By April 2020, Lander had sponsored over 2,254 articles of legislation.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lander |first1=Brad |title=Sponsored Legislation |url=https://legistar.council.nyc.gov/PersonDetail.aspx?ID=42518&GUID=FEE6A879-4718-4990-AFD0-F68A96269855 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |website=The New York City Council |publisher=The NYC Council}}</ref> ''[[City and State New York]]'' ranked Lander's performance in the lower half of all New York City lawmakers, placing him 30th out of the 51 councilmembers; the ranking criteria included number of bills introduced, number of bills signed into law, attendance, and responsiveness to questions from constituents and the media.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lander |first1=Brad |date=January 26, 2020 |title=How we calculated the Best & Worst New York City Lawmakers |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/articles/politics/new-york-city/how-we-calculated-best-worst-new-york-city-lawmakers.html |access-date=April 21, 2020 |work=City & State |issue=analysis of performance}}</ref>

=== Housing ===
Lander opposed rezoning the site of [[Long Island College Hospital]] to include [[affordable housing]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Barbara |last=Eldredge |date=November 20, 2015 |title=Brad Lander Comes Out Against Cobble Hill Rezoning for LICH Development |url=https://www.brownstoner.com/development/brad-lander-comes-cobble-hill-rezoning-lich-development/ |access-date=March 9, 2019 |website=[[Brownstoner Magazine]]}}</ref> In July 2017, he was the primary sponsor of 20 local laws enacted by the City Council and signed by the mayor.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=The New York City Council - Brad S. Lander |url=http://legistar.council.nyc.gov/PersonDetail.aspx?ID=42518&GUID=FEE6A879-4718-4990-AFD0-F68A96269855&Search= |access-date=July 7, 2017 |website=legistar.council.nyc.gov |language=en}}</ref> Lander also played a role in helping shepherd the Community Safety Act through the City Council, along with councilmember [[Jumaane Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Community Safety Act &#124; Communities United for Police Reform |url=https://www.changethenypd.org/community-safety-act |website=www.changethenypd.org}}</ref> In 2017, Lander worked with advocates at the Association of Neighborhood and Housing Development and [[Make the Road New York]] to create a Certificate of No Harassment program that provides the strongest protections against [[tenant harassment]] and displacement of any law in the country.<ref>{{cite web |first=Oscar Perry |last=Abello |date=November 21, 2017 |title=NYC Tenants Rights Advocates Score Another Victory |url=https://nextcity.org/daily/entry/nyc-tenants-right-advocates-score-another-victory |access-date=April 14, 2021 |work=Next City}}</ref> As part of the #TooHotToLearn campaign, Lander led the push to secure air conditioning for all [[New York City Public Schools]] classrooms, shining a spotlight on the 25 percent of classrooms that lacked it.<ref>{{cite web |author=NYC Office of the Mayor |date=April 25, 2017 |title=Mayor de Blasio, Chancellor Fariña and City Council Announce Every Classroom Will Have Air Conditioning by 2022. |url=https://www1.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/261-17/mayor-de-blasio-chancellor-fari-a-city-council-every-classroom-will-have-air |access-date=April 14, 2021 |work=Next City}}</ref>

J. |date=August 10, 2020 |title=Homeless Hotels Creating Chaos on the Upper West Side |url=https://www.jewishpress.com/blogs/the-snag/homeless-hotels-creating-chaos-on-the-upper-west-side/2020/08/10/ |work=The Jewish Press}}</ref> Opponents of the shelters claimed that the contracts contain up to $89 million of unexplained cost compared to contracts for equivalent shelters, and that costs were too Lander's efforts drew intense criticism from Mayor [[Bill de Blasio]]'s [[New York City Human Resources Administration|New York City Department of Social Services]], which Lander called "cartoonish insults".<ref name="Chang-2020" /> The program drew strong reactions from neighborhood residents, with some calling the homeless men "subhuman" and saying the program led to increased crime, open drug sales and drug use, public sex acts, and street harassment, and worrying about the risk of having [[sex offender]]s housed near a public school; other residents were more open to the program, and the owner of a restaurant next door to the hotel reported that, despite some residents' alarm, there had been no problems.<ref>{{cite web |last=Barron |first=Seth |date=December 19, 2020 |title=Progressive leaders make it their mission to afflict comfortable New Yorkers |url=https://nypost.com/2020/12/19/nyc-progressives-make-it-their-mission-to-afflict-the-comfortable/ |work=New York Post}}</ref><ref name="Slotnik-2020" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Waller |first=Derick |date=August 5, 2020 |title=Sex offenders at Upper West Side hotel will likely extend their stay |url=https://abc7ny.com/6345284/ |access-date=August 27, 2020 |website=[[WABC-TV]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Social justice ===
In January 2021, Lander said: "As a white man, [the work of racial justice] starts by listening as honestly as I can to Black people about the anger and pain they are feeling, and the system of [[white supremacy]] and systemic racism it reflects. That is not easy, because it implicates me".<ref name="Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club-2021">{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2021 |title=Candidate Answers to JOLDC: Brad Lander for New York City Comptroller |url=https://jimowles.org/news/candidate-answers-to-joldc-brad-lander-for-new-york-city-comptroller |website=Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club}}</ref> He supported removing the [[Columbus Monument (New York City)|statue of Christopher Columbus]] from [[Columbus Circle]].<ref name="Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club-2021" />

=== Israel and Palestine ===
Lander's council district included large numbers of Jewish and Muslim people. According to ''[[The Forward]]'', Lander has worked to balance relationships with both groups, "befriending both the far-right Brooklyn politician [[Dov Hikind]] and the pro-Palestinian activist and organizer [[Linda Sarsour]]".<ref name="Nathan-Kazis-2017" /> Hikind criticized Lander and other progressive politicians for not distancing themselves from Sarsour, citing her [[criticism of Israel]] and past associations with controversial figures such as [[Louis Farrakhan]].<ref name="Nathan-Kazis-2017" /><ref name="Taylor2014" /><ref>{{cite web |first=Paula |last=Katinas |date=November 28, 2018 |title=Hikind urges progressive pols to speak out against Sarsour |url=https://brooklyneagle.com/articles/2018/11/28/hikind-urges-progressive-pols-to-speak-out-against-sarsour/ |website=[[Brooklyn Eagle]]}}</ref>

In 2020, Lander wrote that he had visited the [[West Bank]] to learn more about conditions under the [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank|Israeli occupation]] and expressed support for efforts to achieve Palestinian human rights.<ref>{{cite web |first=Stephen |last=Witt |date=August 15, 2020 |title=Bklyn Officials Rip DSA For Targeting Israel in Questionnaire |url=https://www.kingscountypolitics.com/bklyn-officials-rip-dsa-for-targeting-israel-in-questionnaire/}}</ref>

In March 2023, Lander wrote an op-ed in the left-wing Israeli newspaper ''[[Haaretz]]'' urging President [[Joe Biden]] and Secretary of State [[Antony Blinken]] to stop providing a "[[Blank cheque|blank check]]" to an "increasingly authoritarian" Israeli government and asking Democrats to stop obeying the [[Pro-Israel lobby in the United States|pro-Israel lobby]] group [[AIPAC]]. He wrote that he participated in a protest outside the Israeli consulate in solidarity with the [[2023 Israeli judicial reform protests]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lander |first=Brad |title=America can't keep writing a blank check to Israel's authoritarian government {{!}} Opinion |url=https://www.haaretz.com/opinion/2023-03-02/ty-article-opinion/.premium/america-cant-keep-writing-a-blank-check-to-israels-authoritarian-government/00000186-a316-de2a-a1ee-a317c9e40000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315035835/https://www.haaretz.com/opinion/2023-03-02/ty-article-opinion/.premium/america-cant-keep-writing-a-blank-check-to-israels-authoritarian-government/00000186-a316-de2a-a1ee-a317c9e40000 |archive-date=March 15, 2023 |access-date=December 11, 2025 |work=[[Haaretz]] |language=en|url-access=registration|url-status=live}}</ref>

Lander split with and left the [[Democratic Socialists of America]] in 2023 following the [[October 7 attacks]].<ref name="Kornbluh"/> In a September 2025 speech, he championed the creation of an alliance "of [[anti-Zionist]]s and [[Liberal Zionism|liberal Zionists]]" seeking to end "the horrors in Gaza" in an appearance with Mamdani before the 2025 mayoral election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strauss |first=Joseph |date=September 11, 2025 |title=Brad Lander calls for 'coalition of anti-Zionists and liberal Zionists' in appearance with Zohran Mamdani |url=https://www.jta.org/2025/09/11/politics/brad-lander-calls-for-coalition-of-anti-zionists-and-liberal-zionists-in-appearance-with-zohran-mamdani |access-date=December 16, 2025 |website=Jewish Telegraphic Agency |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kassel |first=Matthew |date=December 15, 2025 |title=Lander struggles to land hits on Goldman — beyond disagreeing on Israel |url=https://jewishinsider.com/2025/12/brad-lander-dan-goldman-israel-new-york-primary-democratic-party/ |access-date=December 16, 2025 |website=Jewish Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> According to ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'', he is "a liberal Zionist who has called Israel's war in Gaza a genocide and supports conditioning military aid" to Israel.<ref name="Barkan2025"/>

In a December 2025 interview with [[Zeteo]], Lander said that if elected, he would vote to recognize a [[Palestinian state]] and oppose the sale of offensive weapons to Israel. Lander also strongly opposed the censure of U.S. Representative [[Rashida Tlaib]] while calling for U.S. Representative [[Randy Fine]] to be censured for his Islamophobic comments, including calls for genocide of [[American Muslims]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hasan |first=Mehdi |date=January 19, 2026 |title=Trump Is 'Weaponizing' Antisemitism: Brad Lander Speaks to Mehdi |url=https://zeteo.com/p/meet-the-progressive-jewish-critic-israel-brad-lander |access-date=January 21, 2026 |website=zeteo.com |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2026, Lander attended a protest ahead of a speech by Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] at the [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Speri|first=Alice|last2=McMenamin|first2=Lex|date=2026-09-24|title=Netanyahu's speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: 'Let Gaza live'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/24/netanyahu-un-protests|access-date=2026-09-25|work=The Guardian|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Lander was detained along with a group of 90 rabbis and volunteers in the West Bank in October 2026. The entourage, organized by [[Rabbis for Human Rights]], was accompanying Palestinian farmers to harvest olives.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-democratic-congressional-nominee-lander-detained-by-israeli-authorities-west-2026-10-21/ |title=US Democratic congressional candidate Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank |agency=Reuters |date=October 21, 2026}}</ref> The action was similar to previous military closures and international travel denials in response to previous olive harvests, but the detention phase was unusual.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://forward.com/news/843806/israel-west-bank-protective-presence-entry-permits-revoked/ |title=Israel is revoking entry permits for U.S. activists involved in West Bank |author=Theia Chatelle |date=August 7, 2026 |newspaper=[[The Forward]]}}</ref> Activists assert no permits from the military are required for landowners to harvest their own crops in [[Area C]], and that the area was declared to be a closed military zone after they had been harvesting for several days.<ref name="Hunt">{{cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/10/21/nx-s1-6010595/rabbi-detained-by-israeli-forces-in-west-bank-speaks-out |title=Rabbi detained by Israeli forces in West Bank speaks out |date=October 21, 2026 |publisher=[[NPR]] |author1=Alaena Hunt |author2=Matt Ozug |author3=Patrick Jarenwattananon |author4=Scott Detrow}}</ref> Lander was released after several hours, as were the others who were detained.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stack |first1=Liam |title=Israeli Military Detains Brad Lander in West Bank During Volunteer Trip |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/nyregion/brad-lander-west-bank-idf-detained.html?searchResultPosition=1 |access-date=October 22, 2026 |publisher=The New York Times |date=October 21, 2026}}</ref>

=== Public safety and policing ===
In March 2020, as the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City|COVID-19 pandemic]] began, Lander urged that the police suspend criminal arrests, summonses, warrant enforcement, and parole violations for low-level offenses, and release most of the over 900 people incarcerated at [[Rikers Island]] who were over 50 years old.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Public Advocate Jumaane Williams and Council Member Brad Lander Call on City and State Officials to Immediately Halt Broken Windows Arrests and Release Most Rikers Detainees over 50 to Limit Spread of COVID-19 |url=https://council.nyc.gov/brad-lander/2020/03/18/public-advocate-jumaane-williams-and-council-member-brad-lander-call-on-city-and-state-officials-to-immediately-halt-broken-windows-arrests-and-release-most-rikers-detainees-over-50-to-limit-spread-of/ |website=Brad Lander}}</ref> Lander voiced support for [[defunding the police]] and limiting police powers by cutting their budget by $1 billion in 2020.<ref name="LanderNYPD2020">{{Cite web |date=June 10, 2020 |title=New York City council |url=https://council.nyc.gov/brad-lander/2020/06/10/my-commitment-to-working-to-defund-the-nypd |accessdate=March 29, 2021 |work=Brad Lander}}</ref> In December 2020, he called for the disbandment of the [[New York City Police Department]] Vice Unit and for [[decriminalizing prostitution]].<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Joaquin |last1=Sapien |first2=Joshua |last2=Kaplan |date=December 16, 2020 |title=New York Lawmakers Demand NYPD Halt Undercover Sex Trade Stings |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/new-york-lawmakers-demand-nypd-halt-undercover-sex-trade-stings?token=yH0nHeLGUaf_GCiRQKsuaDkneg39WcSL |website=ProPublica}}</ref><ref name="Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club-2021" />

=== Criticism and incidents ===
In May 2016, unnamed Asian-American groups criticized Lander for calling supporters of Yungman Lee, who was challenging [[Nydia Velázquez]] in a House of Representatives election, "scumbags". Lander said he was talking about dark-money entities supporting Lee.<ref>{{cite web |last=Cuba |first=Julianne |date=June 9, 2016 |title=Brad Lander fends off racism accusations |url=https://www.brooklynpaper.com/brad-lander-fends-off-racism-accusations/ |work=[[The Brooklyn Paper]]}}</ref> In December 2017, Lander was arrested at the [[United States Capitol|U.S. Capitol]] while protesting a bill that lowered taxes on corporations and wealthy people while cutting healthcare; he tweeted, "Being arrested with [[Ady Barkan]] in the halls of Congress while ... fighting for a country where we provide health care for those who need it ... is something I'll remember for the rest of my life".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://patch.com/new-york/parkslope/councilman-lander-arrested-protesting-tax-bill-washington|title=Councilman Lander Arrested Protesting Tax Bill In Washington|date=December 14, 2017|website=Park Slope, NY Patch|first=Nicholas|last=Rizzi}}</ref> In June 2018 he was arrested for blocking traffic, disorderly conduct, and failing to disperse at a protest outside the Brooklyn office of State Senator [[Marty Golden]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://brooklyneagle.com/articles/2018/06/29/lander-arrested-at-protest-outside-goldens-office/|title=Lander arrested at protest outside Golden's office|first=Paula |last=Katinas |date=June 29, 2018|website=[[Brooklyn Eagle]]}}</ref>

In 2019, Lander admitted to an [[ethics violation]] for using his official government position to solicit monetary donations for a progressive nonprofit he helped create and of which he was chairman.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sanders |first1=Anna |date=September 13, 2019 |title=NYC Councilman Brad Lander |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/politics/ny-brad-lander-apologizes-ethics-rules-donations-nonprofit-20190913-udmtedrjhrfdvbpkqtfkkah4qi-story.html |access-date=April 21, 2020 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |issue=Apologizes after violating ethics rules}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=pressreader |url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/new-york-daily-news/20190914/281599537200976 |website=The New York Daily News}}</ref> Lander had previously served as chair of the council's Committee on Rules, Privileges and Elections.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |last2= |date=January 22, 2014 |title=Speaker Melissa Mark-Viverito and Rules Committee Chairman Brad Lander Announce Council Leadership and Committee Chairs |url=https://council.nyc.gov/press/2014/01/22/421/ |access-date=January 5, 2026 |website=New York City Council |language=en-US}}</ref> In his second term on the council, he served as the deputy leader for policy.<ref name="GG Comptroller">{{Cite web |url=https://www.gothamgazette.com/city/8228-2021-comptroller-race-now-features-two-city-council-members |title=2021 Comptroller Race Now Features Two City Council Members |date=January 25, 2019 |first1=Samar |last1=Khurshid |website=Gotham Gazette}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Lander lives in Brooklyn with his wife, Meg Barnette, a former executive at [[Planned Parenthood]], now president of Nonprofit New York.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.landerfornyc.com/about-brad|title=About Brad |website=Brad Lander for NYC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://philanthropynewyork.org/news/nonprofit-new-york-announces-new-president-ceo-meg-barnette|title=Nonprofit New York Announces New President & CEO, Meg Barnette|date=March 27, 2020|website=Philanthropy New York}}</ref> He also served as housing chair of Brooklyn Community Board 6, served on the board of directors of the charity [[Jewish Funds for Justice]], and is a [[Little League]] coach in the 78th Precinct Youth Council.<ref name="nation bio">{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2010 |title=Brad Lander |url=https://www.thenation.com/authors/brad-lander/ |work=[[The Nation]]}}</ref>

Lander is a fan of the [[Mike Duncan (podcaster)|''Revolutions'' podcast]] and in relation has described himself as a "[[General Jewish Labour Bund|Bundist]] at heart."<ref>{{Cite Instagram |author= |last=Lander |first=Brad |author-link= |user=brad.lander |postid=DLykgTOttyz |date=July 6, 2025 |title=Great fun meeting @mike_duncan_history of Revolutions Podcast & History of Rome fame. |script-title= |trans-title= |language= |location= |access-date=July 10, 2026 |link=https://www.instagram.com/p/DLykgTOttyz/?igsh=MW9yNjd1OGJvMHY5aA== |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date= |ref=}}</ref>
